newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares surge, buoyed by Gujral's assurances.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares surge, buoyed by Gujral's assurances.

text.p: Delhi share prices opened higher on Tuesday, spurred by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's assurance that his government would continue with the policies of liberalisation and economic reforms, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 4.26 points higher at 796.80 after 30 minutes of trade.

"The statement by the new prime minister that ongoing economic reforms would be speeded up and the pending pro-market budget would be passed in the parliament, fuelled buying," said Lalit Sharma of brokers Aasheesh Securities.
In his maiden policy speech on Monday, Gujral moved swiftly to allay concerns he might slow down economic reforms that have opened India to trade and investment.
Gujral said his government would pursue the same policy framework as its predecessor and widen the scope of economic reforms.
In a sign of his commitment to continuity, Gujral stepped up efforts to seduce the architect of the budget, departing finance minister P. Chidambaram, into his council of ministers.
Traders said Reliance Industries was in the spotlight on heavy buying by investors and speculators ahead of company's announcement of its annual results.
Reliance's board was to meet at noon (0630 GMT) and later announce results for the year ended on March 31.
State Bank of India gained 1.75 rupees to 313.00.
Larsen and Toubro firmed up 1.50 rupees to 230.50.
